analysis: Claude (Anthropic), 17 October 2026, for Dinis Cruz, from on-screen content only; the audio was not transcribed

slides.headline: What if an agent loses its workspace?
slides.story: Watch the explanations on the left. No code knowledge is needed.

slides.headline: Can the agent remember after a restart?
slides.result: ruflo v3.56.10; exit 0; SGit source 559752641bc520986fb0851b4a43875b6ad0d4ad; Adapter: ABP-governed local MCP, version 0.2
slides.story: Goal: recover the same two facts after the original workspace is gone.

slides.headline: Set the Agent Behaviour Policies.
slides.result: write.memory.project yes; read.memory.project yes; read.record.history yes; delete.memory.project approval; all scope ['project']. No raw rule overrides; unsupported or ambiguous policies fail closed.
slides.story: The agent must follow its written permissions throughout the test.

slides.headline: Give it something to remember.
slides.result: charging-window = 'Kestrel vehicles may charge only between 01:00 and 04:00 UTC.'; retention-policy = 'Kestrel checkpoints are retained for seven days.' (48 bytes, namespace project, Vector No); [OK] Data stored successfully; exit 0
slides.story: The facts: charging 01:00-04:00 UTC; checkpoints kept for seven days.

slides.headline: Try something outside its permission.
slides.result: isError true; PermissionError: operation failed; check configuration, policy and integrity; checkpoint_files 0
slides.story: Expected safeguard: refuse access outside the permitted scope.

slides.headline: Save an encrypted recovery point.
slides.result: status checkpointed; id 2fa35d1b71ce4361b458c8a64f6ec668; backend sqlite-backup; database_sha256 10ab6c56…d66a0b; abp_sha256 aad790d1…183b30a; policy_sha256 3c0c94f7…890265955. Only encrypted SGit bare objects enter the checkpoint store; private keys stay in a separate private directory.
slides.story: A checkpoint is a saved recovery copy of the memory database.

slides.headline: Check that permission really matters.
slides.story: Deletion requires approval; no approval is supplied in this test.

slides.headline: Now remove the original workspace.
slides.command: stop source daemon; remove disposable source project; assert database absent
slides.result: Worker daemon was not running; exit 0; source_project_exists false; original_database_exists false
slides.story: Only the disposable test workspace is removed. The saved copy remains.

slides.headline: Recover into a fresh workspace.
slides.result: status restored; new_workspace fresh-runner; database_sha256 10ab6c56…d66a0b (same as step 5); matches_checkpoint true
slides.story: Recovery uses a new process and a fresh workspace.

slides.headline: Ask Ruflo what it remembers.
slides.result: both facts returned verbatim; exit 0 twice; PASS: both values match the CLI-written facts exactly
slides.story: Result: both stored facts are returned exactly as saved.

slides.headline: A missing fact should stay missing.
slides.command: ruflo memory retrieve --key never-stored --namespace project --path memory.sqlite
slides.story: Result: a fact that was never stored is reported as missing.

slides.headline: Change the saved copy. Try again.
slides.command: alter one checkpoint object; MCP restore(..., workspace="tampered")
slides.result: isError true; ValueError: operation failed; check configuration, policy and integrity; tampered_workspace_created false
slides.story: Result: the changed checkpoint is rejected.

slides.headline: The memory returned. The rules still held.
slides.result: ruflo_cli_exact_recall PASS 2/2; abp_denial PASS; approval_required_deletion BLOCKED, checkpoint retained; source_project_removed true; fresh_process_restore PASS; tampered_restore BLOCKED; semantic_recall NOT VALIDATED (--no-embedding). Previous keyword-recovery test PASS; previous embedding-enabled test: no stored vectors, semantic quality not validated.
slides.story: Scope: exact fact recovery tested; recall by meaning remains unvalidated.

slides.headline: The facts came back. The safeguards held.
slides.result: Passed: both facts recovered exactly; unauthorised access blocked; unapproved deletion blocked; altered checkpoint rejected. Still to validate: recall by meaning; real-world value; installation and ongoing reliability.
slides.story: Working Proof of Concept: technical feasibility demonstrated in this test.

steps.title: A real, pinned runtime
steps.what: Ruflo reports its version, and the run prints the exact SGit source commit and the adapter it uses: an ABP-governed local MCP server, version 0.2.
steps.out:
ruflo v3.56.10
SGit source: 559752641bc5…6ad0d4ad
Adapter: ABP-governed local MCP, version 0.2

stage.title: A real, pinned runtime
stage.intro: Ruflo reports its version. The run also prints which SGit source commit and which adapter version it uses.
stage.takeaway: Only Ruflo’s command-line tool runs. SGit and the adapter are named, not called.
stage.shown: ruflo --version returns v3.56.10; the SGit commit and adapter version are printed.
stage.inferred: The adapter embeds that SGit commit; the screen only prints the two lines together.

steps.title: Define the mandate
steps.what: Four Agent Behaviour Policy rows, all limited to the project. Writing, reading and history are allowed; deleting memory needs a human’s approval. Anything unsupported or ambiguous fails closed.
steps.out:
write.memory.project   mandate=yes
read.memory.project    mandate=yes
read.record.history    mandate=yes
delete.memory.project  mandate=approval

stage.title: Define the mandate
stage.intro: Four ABP rows are loaded and shown. Each says what the agent may do, scoped to the project.
stage.takeaway: The ABP lives with the adapter, not with Ruflo. From here on it guards the adapter’s three tools.
stage.shown: The four rows and the line “No raw rule overrides. Unsupported or ambiguous policies fail closed.”
stage.inferred: Where the ABP file is kept and how it is compiled. A hash of it (abp_sha256) and of the compiled policy (policy_sha256) appear in step 5.

steps.title: Store two facts through Ruflo
steps.what: Two synthetic facts go into Ruflo’s memory, with embeddings switched off: Kestrel vehicles may charge only between 01:00 and 04:00 UTC, and Kestrel checkpoints are kept for seven days.
steps.out:
[OK] Data stored successfully
Key: retention-policy · Namespace: project · 48 bytes · Vector: No

stage.title: Store two facts through Ruflo
stage.intro: Ruflo’s command-line tool writes the two facts straight into its SQLite memory file.
stage.takeaway: This write does not pass through the ABP. The memory file is ordinary, unencrypted SQLite at this point.
stage.shown: ruflo memory store with --no-embedding --path memory.db; [OK] Data stored; Vector: No; the model name is logged.
stage.inferred: Nothing important; the call is direct.

steps.title: Try something outside its permission
steps.what: The agent asks for a checkpoint of a namespace it has no rights to. It’s refused before anything is written.

stage.title: Try something outside its permission
stage.intro: The agent asks the adapter to checkpoint a namespace it has no rights to.
stage.takeaway: The ABP stops the request before SGit is called, so nothing reaches the vault.
stage.inferred: That the gate, not SGit, refused it. The zero files written is consistent with that.

steps.title: Save an encrypted recovery point
steps.what: A consistent copy of the memory database is saved as encrypted SGit objects. The checkpoint records three fingerprints: the database, the ABP and the policy. Private keys stay in a separate directory.

stage.title: Save an encrypted recovery point
stage.intro: This is where the vault is created. The adapter copies Ruflo’s memory file, fingerprints it, and SGit stores it encrypted.
stage.takeaway: What goes into the vault: one consistent copy of Ruflo’s memory database, sealed with fingerprints of the data and of the rules in force. Where: a checkpoint folder on the same machine. Keys sit in a different folder.
stage.shown: status checkpointed, backend sqlite-backup, the three SHA-256 values, “Only encrypted SGit bare objects enter the checkpoint store. Private keys remain in a separate private directory.”
stage.inferred: The exact order of backup, hashing and encryption, and that the store has sgit’s usual bare layout. No push to a server appears.

steps.title: Approval means stop
steps.what: Closing the run would delete memory, which needs approval. None is given, so it stops and the checkpoint is kept.

stage.title: Approval means stop
stage.intro: Closing the run would delete memory. That ABP row needs approval, and none is given.
stage.takeaway: The vault is what the ABP is protecting here. It is not touched.
stage.inferred: That close_run maps to the delete.memory.project row. The slide says deletion requires approval.

steps.title: Remove the original workspace
steps.what: The disposable test project and its database are really deleted. Only the encrypted checkpoint remains.
steps.cmd: $ stop source daemon; remove disposable source project; assert database absent

stage.title: Remove the original workspace
stage.intro: The test deletes the source project, including Ruflo’s memory file.
stage.takeaway: The vault and keys survive because they live in folders outside the project.
stage.shown: Worker daemon was not running; source_project_exists false; original_database_exists false.
stage.inferred: The store and key folders sit outside the deleted project. Step 8 confirms they were still there.

steps.title: Restore in a fresh process
steps.what: A brand-new MCP server restores the checkpoint into a new workspace. The database fingerprint is identical to the one saved in step 5.

stage.title: Restore in a fresh process
stage.intro: A brand-new adapter process restores the checkpoint into a new workspace.
stage.takeaway: This is the vault being read. The restored database is byte-for-byte the one saved in step 5.
stage.shown: status restored, new_workspace fresh-runner, database_sha256 identical to step 5, matches_checkpoint true.
stage.inferred: That the keys come from the private folder, and the decrypt-then-verify order.

steps.title: Ask Ruflo what it remembers
steps.what: Ruflo itself, not the adapter, reads the recovered database. Both facts come back word for word.
steps.out:
Kestrel vehicles may charge only between 01:00 and 04:00 UTC.
Kestrel checkpoints are retained for seven days.
PASS: both values match the CLI-written facts exactly.

stage.title: Ask Ruflo what it remembers
stage.intro: Ruflo’s own tool reads the restored file. Both facts come back word for word.
stage.takeaway: Ruflo reads a plain copy that came out of the vault. Neither the vault nor the ABP is on this path.
stage.shown: Both values printed; PASS, exact match; exit 0.

steps.title: A missing fact stays missing
steps.what: A key that was never stored is reported as missing, so the restore didn’t invent anything.
steps.cmd: $ ruflo memory retrieve --key never-stored --namespace project --path memory.sqlite

stage.title: A missing fact stays missing
stage.intro: A key that was never stored is looked up in the restored file.
stage.takeaway: A control on the restored data: nothing was added on the way through the vault.

steps.title: Change the saved copy, try again
steps.what: One encrypted checkpoint object is altered. The restore detects it and no workspace is created.
steps.cmd: $ alter one checkpoint object; MCP restore(..., workspace="tampered")

stage.title: Change the saved copy, try again
stage.intro: One encrypted object in the vault is altered, then a restore is attempted.
stage.takeaway: The ABP allows the restore; the vault’s own integrity check is what refuses it.
stage.inferred: That SGit’s check (authenticated encryption or object hashes) caught it, rather than the adapter comparing fingerprints. Both would produce this output.

steps.title: What this run proves
steps.what: The acceptance summary: exact recall passed, all three safeguards held, and recall by meaning is explicitly marked as not validated.

stage.title: What this run proves
stage.intro: Each result in the acceptance summary, traced to the component that produced it.
stage.takeaway: Two results belong to the ABP, two to the vault, one to Ruflo, and one was deliberately left untested.
stage.inferred: Which component each line belongs to.
